subsystems.name: Engineered microbial chassis
subsystems.role: Performs the desired atmospheric chemistry — fixing carbon, releasing oxygen or consuming unwanted gases.

subsystems.name: Nutrient and resource supply
subsystems.role: Provides the nitrogen, phosphorus and trace metals microbes need to grow.

subsystems.name: Environmental conditioning
subsystems.role: Makes the surface survivable for the microbes — warming, shielding and creating liquid water.

subsystems.name: Dispersal and colonisation system
subsystems.role: Spreads the organisms across a planet and helps them establish.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and control
subsystems.role: Tracks atmospheric change and keeps the organisms contained and safe.

subsystems.name: Planetary protection and containment
subsystems.role: Prevents contamination of Earth and other bodies, and ensures reversibility.

buildSteps.title: Define the target atmosphere
buildSteps.detail: Choose a planet and specify the end state: pressure, temperature and gas mix that would allow liquid water and breathable air.

buildSteps.title: Identify the metabolic pathway
buildSteps.detail: Find or design enzymes that convert the existing atmosphere (e.g. carbon dioxide) into the desired products (e.g. oxygen) using energy from sunlight or chemical gradients.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the microbe
buildSteps.detail: Use synthetic biology — gene synthesis, CRISPR editing and directed evolution — to insert these pathways into a hardy chassis and add radiation and desiccation tolerance.

buildSteps.title: Test in simulated planetary conditions
buildSteps.detail: Grow the organisms in chambers that mimic low pressure, cold, radiation and toxic soil chemistry, iterating until they survive and function.

buildSteps.title: Design delivery and dispersal
buildSteps.detail: Build landers that can safely transport dormant microbes and release them where they can find nutrients and shelter, such as subsurface ice deposits.

buildSteps.title: Establish a seed colony
buildSteps.detail: Deploy the first microbes in a protected niche — a crater, cave or polar ice — where they can multiply without being killed by ultraviolet light or vacuum.

buildSteps.title: Scale up and let them spread
buildSteps.detail: As the colony grows, it produces gases and modifies the soil, gradually creating conditions for further spread across the planet.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and control
buildSteps.detail: Use orbiting and surface instruments to track gas levels, and keep genetic kill switches ready in case the process must be halted.

buildSteps.title: Iterate with new traits
buildSteps.detail: Introduce additional engineered organisms to fix nitrogen, build soil or produce water, compounding the atmospheric change over centuries.

prerequisites.why: we can already rewrite microbial genomes, but building a fully synthetic organism for a new environment is far beyond current practice.
organisms exist that tolerate radiation, cold and salt, but none thrives on a raw planetary surface.
growing microbes on a planet requires extracting water, nitrogen and minerals locally.
we can simulate atmospheres, but long-term biological feedbacks are poorly understood.
international rules already govern contamination, though not for deliberate large-scale release.
initial habitats and delivery systems would need to be built without human presence.

pathway.milestone: lab research on synthetic minimal cells and extremophiles
pathway.unlocks: basic understanding of what it takes for life to survive off Earth.

pathway.milestone: robotic missions that test microbial survival on Mars or in low Earth orbit
pathway.unlocks: real data on radiation, perchlorates and low pressure.

pathway.milestone: small-scale contained demonstration in a planetary analogue
pathway.unlocks: proof that an engineered organism can alter a closed atmosphere.

pathway.milestone: first deliberate release on a planetary surface
pathway.unlocks: the start of a centuries-long terraforming process.
a breathable atmosphere and liquid water — if the biology holds.
